title: Top-Spending Customers (Derived Table)
description:
Use a **subquery in the FROM clause** (derived table) to first calculate each customer's total spend, then return customers who have spent more than 200.

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `status`, `total_amount`

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`, `email`, `city`, `country`

Output columns: `name`, `total_spend`. Order by `total_spend` descending.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, country VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@example.com','New York','USA'),(2,'Bob','bob@example.com','London','UK'),(3,'Carol','carol@example.com','Chicago','USA'),(4,'Dan','dan@example.com','Mumbai','India'); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, total_amount DECIMAL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,DATE '2026-01-05','completed',100.00),(2,1,DATE '2026-02-10','completed',150.00),(3,2,DATE '2026-01-06','completed',80.00),(4,3,DATE '2026-01-07','completed',300.00),(5,4,DATE '2026-01-08','completed',50.00);
solution_sql: SELECT c.name, t.total_spend FROM (SELECT customer_id, SUM(total_amount) AS total_spend FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) t JOIN customers c ON t.customer_id = c.id WHERE t.total_spend > 200 ORDER BY total_spend DESC
hints: A subquery in FROM acts like a temporary table: FROM (SELECT ...) alias.
You can then JOIN and WHERE filter against it like any regular table.
explanation: The inner query sums orders per customer. The outer query joins this derived table to customers and filters by total_spend > 200. Alice spent 100+150=250; Carol spent 300. Bob (80) and Dan (50) are excluded.
